title: Uncertainty & Risk
headline_read: Policy uncertainty is high — what governments do next is a major source of risk.

indicators.title: U.S. Economic Policy Uncertainty
indicators.context: The Baker/Bloom/Davis index of U.S. economic policy uncertainty, built by counting newspaper coverage of policy-driven economic uncertainty. The long-run norm is about 100; it spikes around elections, debt-ceiling standoffs, trade wars, and crises.
indicators.read: U.S. policy uncertainty is at 244 — far above its long-run norm of about 100.

indicators.title: Global Economic Policy Uncertainty
indicators.context: The same newspaper-based uncertainty measure aggregated across 21 countries (GDP-weighted). Note: it publishes with a lag of about six months, so it reads as a sanity check on the timelier U.S. index above, not a live signal.
indicators.read: Global policy uncertainty is at 278 — far above its long-run norm of about 100.
